newsitem.title: USA: Russian resupply ship launched to Mir, NASA.
newsitem.headline: Russian resupply ship launched to Mir, NASA.

text.p: A cargo spaceship was launched on Saturday to deliver crucial repair gear and supplies to Russia's stricken Mir space station, a NASA spokesman said.

The Progress resupply ship blasted off the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan shortly after midnight EDT (0400 GMT), NASA spokesman John Lawrence said. The craft is due to dock with the orbiting outpost on Monday.

The 7-ton spaceship is carrying equipment to restore some of the power lost when an earlier Progress craft ploughed into Mir on June 25, badly damaging a science module called Spektr and robbing the station of half its power supply.
Mir cosmonauts Vasili Tsbiliev and Alexander Lazutkin are to make a spacewalk inside the station no earlier than July 17 or 18 to connect cables to Spektr's electricity-generating solar panels.
NASA's Mir resident, Michael Foale, will sit out the repair inside the station's emergency escape vehicle in case the work goes wrong.
The Progress is to dock with Mir at 1:58 a.m. EDT (0558 GMT) under computer control. Last month's orbital collision occurred when the Progress was being controlled manually.
